svg.text: LATENT INFORMATION ARCHAEOLOGY / PART I / I-04. THE COST OF A CONNECTION
Producing a record is cheap next to connecting it
The arithmetic of pairs, one mechanism, and three measurements, all made through citations
LIA could be formalized around an economic premise: the marginal cost of generating information has historically been lower
than the aggregate cost of connecting all available information.
Every new artifact adds n possible pairs
one unit of work for its
cost of connecting all of them
As long as people produce steadily and can read only so much, the unexamined
share rises. A backlog accumulates without anyone neglecting anything.
Two costs that move in opposite directions
Hsieh measured usefulness by later citations, for 18,882 inventions selected from
2.14 million US patents granted from 1975 to 1993.

The lag has been getting shorter. A patent citation records attention or use; it

Scored by whether a material later appeared beside thermoelectric terms: what

This is a research proposition, not an established universal law.
